title: G29-62 Happy Teenager Walla
creator: USC Gold Library (1930s-40s Hollywood optical sound effects)
notes: Dense, steady room of teenagers chatting (a different recording from chatter.mp3); no dominant speaker is visible in the level or spectrum. The optical source is band-limited to about 8 kHz. title: R26-07 Large Wooden Object Dragged on Wood Floor (single drag)
creator: USC Red Library
notes: Single ~1.4 s wooden drag with stick-slip judder (a chair or desk scraped on a wooden floor), 2.75-4.4 s of source; head trimmed, 120 ms fade-out; -14 LUFS. Source: USC Optical Sound Effects Library / Sunset Editorial Library (Craig Smith collection), published by the Internet Archive with a CC0 1.0 dedication.

title: Desk drumming loop (assembled from R22-35 Wood Foley - Hollow Flat Surface)
creator: USC Red Library (source hits); loop assembled for this project
notes: No rhythmic desk-drumming recording with a clean PD/CC0 licence was found, so single palm thumps, knuckle knocks and ghost taps on a hollow wooden surface, cut from this CC0 foley take, were sequenced into a 4-bar groove at 104 bpm (slight timing and velocity humanising, hit tails wrapped round the loop point, source room tone underneath). Loops seamlessly; -18 LUFS. Source: USC Optical Sound Effects Library / Sunset Editorial Library (Craig Smith collection), published by the Internet Archive with a CC0 1.0 dedication.

title: Pencil tapping loop (assembled from R22-35 Wood Foley - Hollow Flat Surface)
creator: USC Red Library (source taps); loop assembled for this project
notes: Short hard taps on wood from this CC0 foley take, high-passed (~1.4 kHz) and shortened to a dry 'tk' click, then sequenced as a restless tapping pattern (~8 taps/s in bursts). Seamless loop. Very peaky, so about -20 LUFS at TP -1.5 dBTP. This is a built arrangement: no clean PD/CC0 pencil-tap recording was found. Source: USC Optical Sound Effects Library / Sunset Editorial Library (Craig Smith collection), published by the Internet Archive with a CC0 1.0 dedication.

title: Reveille (bugle call)
creator: United States Army Band
license: Public domain (work of the U.S. federal government, PD-USGov-Military-Army)
notes: Full US Army 'Reveille' on solo bugle; head silence trimmed, natural tail with a 250 ms fade; mono (source band-limited to ~11.5 kHz); -14 LUFS.

title: The Stars and Stripes Forever (Edison Amberol cylinder 4M-285)
creator: Sousa's Band (comp. John Philip Sousa, d.1932)
license: Public domain (1909 recording, PD-US-record-expired; composer d.1932)
notes: Excerpt 4.37-60.82 s = first strain (x2) + second strain (x2). The loop point jumps from the end of strain 2 back to the first strain's downbeat (like a da capo), found by self-similarity and beat alignment, with a 60 ms equal-power crossfade. Acoustic-era surface noise retained; mono; -18 LUFS. NPS catalogue EDIS 36682, click-removed transfer.

title: R16-41 Typewriter Roller Movements (single carriage slam)
creator: USC Red Library
notes: Single sharp typewriter carriage/roller slam with a short mechanical rattle (0.50-1.08 s of source), for use as a 'stamp' thud; head trimmed; -14 LUFS. No clean PD/CC0 rubber-stamp recording was found. Source: USC Optical Sound Effects Library / Sunset Editorial Library (Craig Smith collection), published by the Internet Archive with a CC0 1.0 dedication.
